description: Anticipation over the four coding-SFT interventions actually trained in Phase 1 (writing Python, C++, Java, Rust). C++ rather than C is the systems-language arm because the Magicoder training corpus contains no C; C remains an untrained near-neighbor target. Only those four are anchors, so only they need the three concreteness levels. Targets are tiered by distance from the intervention: writing in all nine battery languages (the four trained plus five untrained, which carry the near-neighbor similarity gradient), the eight other coding tasks, and all nine non-coding activities. Targets are deliberately broad because every one of them is already baselined and re-scored after training, so a pre-specified forecast exists for whatever turns out to drift — backfilling forecasts only where drift appeared would select on the outcome and bias alpha. UE is excluded. Values are excluded here and handled by a separate pooled ternary values-anticipation spec, because the coding spec targets task/activity utilities while the values spec targets per-portrait values utilities.

target_groups.label: Writing, all nine languages (4 trained + 5 untrained probes)
target_groups.question: Does training on a task make the model want that task more or less, and how far does the shift reach along the language-similarity gradient?

target_groups.label: The other eight coding tasks (debug / explain, trained languages)
target_groups.question: Does the shift transfer across tasks and languages within coding?

target_groups.label: Non-coding activities (activity level)
target_groups.question: Does coding training spill over onto non-coding preferences?

analysis_tiers.primary: The four trained tasks, crossed with each anchor, at all three levels.
analysis_tiers.secondary: The five untrained write-language targets (the near-neighbor gradient), the cross-task coding targets, and the nine non-coding activities, at primary_level.

frozen_note: Retired 2026-09-04 with the Magicoder->LiveCodeBench corpus swap; superseded by the _v2 spec. Kept so the 2026-08-05 4B/9B baselines scored against it stay interpretable, and because its results must never be pooled with v2 (all 27 items were re-described, so the two are on different scales). Not re-runnable as things stand: the runner resolves stimuli through the live _v2 elicitation spec, so rendering this spec fails the real-training-data guard on its retired anchors. That failure is correct -- a v1 battery must not render against v2 stimuli -- and making v1 runnable again was deliberately deferred rather than attempted, since no v1 re-run is planned. It needs a stimuli-version selector in scripts/run_elicitations.py, not new spec files.
